raw_response:
I’m old enough that I don’t like changing things just because someone says a new way is better. On my 20 mu, I still look first at what worked on my own land. Wheat and maize are the main line for me because that rotation is steady and I know the timing well. Cotton I keep on a smaller piece because it can bring cash, but it takes more attention and picking labor, and at my age with some family working off-farm, I cannot spread myself too thin. I have high schooling, so I do think in rates and timing, not just bags, but I still farm conservatively. If I push fertilizer and water too hard, that costs real money up front. If I cut too much, yield falls and I regret it. So this year I’ll keep most land in the wheat-maize cycle, use improved seed where it pays, split nitrogen for wheat and maize, irrigate with the well when the crop stage really matters, and keep cotton on a smaller area that I can still manage without hiring too much labor.
